panels.title: Real yield against gold
panels.mechanism: Gold pays nothing, so its only competitor is an inflation-protected bond. When the real yield falls, holding gold costs less and gold rises. So the mechanism predicts these two move in OPPOSITE directions.
panels.note: The master relationship. Everything else is a branch of it.
panels.expect_text: negative — the two should move opposite

panels.title: Oil against inflation expectations
panels.mechanism: Oil is an input to nearly every price. When it rises the market raises its inflation forecast, which is what breakeven measures. The mechanism predicts these move TOGETHER.
panels.note: Oil → inflation expectations → central bank → real yields → gold.
panels.expect_text: positive — the two should move together

panels.title: The dollar against gold
panels.mechanism: Commodities are priced in dollars worldwide. A stronger dollar makes the same ounce dearer for every foreign buyer, so demand falls. The mechanism predicts these move in OPPOSITE directions.
panels.expect_text: negative — the two should move opposite

panels.title: Real yield against the risk ladder
panels.mechanism: Every asset competes for the same savings and the real yield is the referee. High real yields make safety attractive and money leaves the top of the ladder. The mechanism predicts these move in OPPOSITE directions.
panels.expect_text: negative — the two should move opposite

panels.title: The yield curve as early warning
panels.mechanism: An inverted curve is a LAGGED warning, typically six to eighteen months ahead. There is no reliable same-day relationship, so expect the correlation strip to look like noise. Judge this one from the scorecard, not from this chart.
panels.note: The near-zero R² here is the honest reading: contemporaneously, the curve tells you almost nothing about equities. The strip is left uncoloured because there is no same-day claim to pass or fail.
panels.expect_text: none — this mechanism makes no same-day prediction

scorecard.name: Real yield deeply low
scorecard.desc: Real yield more than 1σ below its two-year mean.

scorecard.name: Real yield stretched high
scorecard.desc: Real yield more than 1σ above its mean; bonds outcompeting gold.

scorecard.name: Curve inverted → equities fall in 1y
scorecard.desc: NOTE: the curve's real claim is about RECESSIONS, not equity prices. This tests the weaker equity version because recession dates are not in this dataset.

scorecard.name: Gold stretched
scorecard.desc: Gold more than 2σ above its own one-year mean. A mean-reversion test.

scorecard.name: Dollar falling hard
scorecard.desc: Dollar down more than 4% over 90 days.

fragility.label: Moderate
fragility.disclosure: Unvalidated heuristic. Components are equally weighted and the mappings from raw values to 0–1 scores were chosen by hand, not fitted or backtested. Treat this as a rough summary of several readings, not as a measured quantity.
